purpose: Expected educational scenarios, NOT scanner results
limitations: Semgrep and Trivy were not installed in the existing security environment.
Official advisory and rule metadata verification is not proof of scanner detection.
The central pipeline uses Snyk Code, not Semgrep CE, and does not load local Semgrep rules.
Patched versions below fix the named CVE only; they are not a guarantee of freedom from other CVEs.
Additional findings, duplicate locations and severity differences are expected.

scenarios.description: Untrusted text is interpolated into a SQLite SQL statement.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Use a SQL placeholder and pass the username as a bound parameter.

scenarios.description: Untrusted text is concatenated into a shell command with shell=True.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Avoid the shell and pass an argument list to a fixed executable.

scenarios.description: A filename is combined with a base directory without confinement validation.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Resolve both paths and reject paths outside the allowed base directory.

scenarios.description: MD5 is used as a password digest.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Use a password KDF such as Argon2id or scrypt with a random per-password salt.

scenarios.description: A clearly fictional, unused demonstration password is embedded in a function.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Read real credentials from a secret manager or injected environment variable.

scenarios.description: An untrusted value is assigned directly to innerHTML.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Use textContent for plain text or a reviewed sanitizer when HTML is necessary.

scenarios.description: Session connection reuse can retain disabled TLS verification.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Upgrade to a maintained compatible requests version, at least 2.32.0 for this CVE.

scenarios.description: Catastrophic backtracking in URL authority parsing can cause denial of service.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Upgrade to a maintained compatible urllib3 version, at least 1.26.5 for this CVE.

scenarios.description: Unsafe YAML construction can allow arbitrary code execution.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Upgrade to a maintained compatible PyYAML version, at least 5.4 for this CVE, and use safe_load.

scenarios.description: The template API can permit command injection.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Upgrade to a maintained lodash version, at least 4.17.21 for this CVE, and regenerate the lockfile.

scenarios.description: Argument parsing is vulnerable to prototype pollution.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Upgrade to a maintained minimist version, at least 1.2.6 on this branch, and regenerate the lockfile.

scenarios.description: HTML manipulation with untrusted input can result in XSS.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Upgrade to a maintained jQuery version, at least 3.5.0 for this CVE, and regenerate the lockfile.

scenarios.description: The VPC default security group permits all ingress including SSH from IPv4/IPv6 world CIDRs, and unrestricted egress.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Remove default-group rules and use dedicated groups with minimal ports and trusted CIDRs.

scenarios.description: S3 public ACL blocking is disabled.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Enable block_public_acls and ignore_public_acls and remove the public ACL.

scenarios.description: S3 public policy blocking and public bucket restriction are disabled.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Enable block_public_policy and restrict_public_buckets.

scenarios.description: A public-read ACL and an anonymous s3:GetObject policy expose the fictional bucket.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Use a private bucket without public ACLs and grant read access only to approved principals.

scenarios.description: The EBS volume explicitly has encrypted=false.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Enable EBS encryption and configure an appropriate managed encryption key.

scenarios.description: The container is privileged.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Set privileged=false and remove unnecessary Linux capabilities.

scenarios.description: The workload explicitly runs with UID 0.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Set runAsNonRoot=true and an appropriate nonzero runAsUser UID.

scenarios.description: A ClusterRole grants wildcard API groups, resources and verbs to the lab service account.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Use a namespaced Role with the minimum resources and verbs and a matching RoleBinding.

scenarios.description: allowPrivilegeEscalation is explicitly enabled.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Set allowPrivilegeEscalation=false.

scenarios.description: The container root filesystem is writable.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Set readOnlyRootFilesystem=true and use explicit temporary volumes where required.

scenarios.description: All Linux capabilities are added and defaults are not dropped.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Drop ALL capabilities and add only individually justified capabilities.

scenarios.description: The workload has no CPU or memory requests and limits.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Define workload-appropriate CPU and memory requests and limits.

scenarios.description: An unnecessary service account token is automatically mounted.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Set automountServiceAccountToken=false when API access is unnecessary.

scenarios.description: The backend Dockerfile does not select a non-root USER.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Create or select an unprivileged user and set USER explicitly.

scenarios.description: The backend Dockerfile has no HEALTHCHECK; this is a low-risk hardening fixture, not an exploit.
scenarios.recommended_fix: For a long-running service, add a meaningful HEALTHCHECK; a one-shot banner may legitimately omit it.

scenarios.description: The frontend Dockerfile does not select the available non-root node USER.
scenarios.recommended_fix: Set USER node before the entrypoint.

scenarios.description: The frontend Dockerfile has no HEALTHCHECK; this is a hardening fixture for static analysis.
scenarios.recommended_fix: For a long-running service, add a meaningful HEALTHCHECK; document exemptions for one-shot workloads.
